verdict: Lend selectively in Nagpur engineering and capital goods: OK for OEM and component makers with order visibility and stable power, avoid EPC and power-intensive units until receivables and supply quality are proven.
title: Nagpur Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Engineering and capital goods in Nagpur means metal cutting, fabrication, castings, machining and small assemblies sold to OEMs, railways, power and infra buyers.** Cash comes in on dispatch, but the buyer sets the payment clock; the unit funds raw material and wages in between. **Value sits in the order book and the customer relationship, not the machine on the floor** [5][6]. Pricing power is thin for job-work units and better for proprietary component makers; capex is lumpy and funded ahead of revenue [4][11].

## What has changed now
**The national demand signal is strong: IIP NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date, with exports +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD** [D]. Maharashtra GST collections are +8.6% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, so the local tax base is growing faster than the country [D]. **The local constraint is power quality, not demand:** MIDC Industries Association has asked MSEDCL for more transformer capacity and new substations, citing dips and fluctuations that damage CNC machines and motors [3]. So when a proposal lands, check the unit's feeder and backup; if it runs sensitive CNC without stabilisation, ask for the downtime log and the insurance cover.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue component and sub-assembly makers feeding data centres, mining, off-highway, railways and transmission** — peers report record order books and export growth in exactly these lines [4][6]. **Pursue exporters and Tier-2 suppliers to large OEMs**, since export momentum is running at +19.8% Apr-to-date [D]. **Avoid pure EPC and long-execution contractors** unless receivables are clean: peers show revenue growth without margin — Suzlon's EBITDA margin narrowed to 14.8% from 18.6% [7], and EPC cash conversion cycles run longer than OEMs [11]. Local news on Nagpur MSMEs is thin [1][2], so lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Take monthly stock and receivable statements, and a monthly power-outage log for CNC-heavy units [3]. **Ask for the order book with buyer names and delivery dates** — DEE's order book crossed Rs 1,300 crore with revenue up 77% YoY to Rs 286.7 crore [5]; that is the visibility we want to see replicated. **Price for the guarantee burden:** bank guarantees for bidding tie up limits [9], so size non-fund limits separately and review utilisation monthly.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days stretching past the stated credit terms, inventory building without matching orders, and repeated power-related production losses** [3][9]. **Watch margin compression despite volume growth** — the Suzlon pattern of 26% revenue growth with flat EBITDA at Rs 720 crore [7] is the signal to reprice or exit. **Watch order book concentration:** if one buyer is over half the book, ask for the contract and payment history before renewal.
watch: Receivable days exceed stated terms for two months -> freeze enhancement, ask for buyer confirmations
More than routine dips damaging machines -> require stabiliser or backup before renewal [3]
Quarterly order book and buyer concentration
Single buyer above half the book -> seek contract copy and diversify or reduce limit
Utilisation near limit with slow billing -> resize limits, review pricing [9]
Margin falls while revenue rises -> reprice or exit, per peer pattern [7]
